The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

A Hello You Can Fold

Caty was trying out welcomes by the crooked roof. Chip liked a clap of wings. Toad liked a bump of elbows, although nobody could say for certain where his elbows were. Mouse liked to be asked.

Then came Hedgehog. “Everybody Day sounds lovely,” she said. “I should like to say hello from about here.” About here was the other side of a watering can. Caty wondered how a hello could reach that far.

Chip tried a very loud “HELLO!” A blackbird three gardens over called hello back. Hedgehog curled into a bristly ball. From inside came a small, perfectly clear voice. “A little less hello, please.”

Caty sat where she was. After a while one bright eye peeked out. Caty raised a wing. Hedgehog raised a paw. It was such a small paw that Caty nearly missed it. She raised her wing again.

Hedgehog uncurling was like a brush becoming a face. “That one felt right,” she said. Caty folded her wing and opened it slowly, like a paper fan. Hedgehog opened her paw and spread every toe.

Mouse tried the fan hello. Toad tried it. He opened so many toes he toppled backward into the watering can’s saucer. Hedgehog laughed a laugh that reached all the way across the gap.

Caty drew two wings on a paper leaf for the Welcome Tree. One folded, one open. Visitors could wave if they liked. When Hedgehog passed under the branch, she gave it a tiny, private pawful of hello.

At home that evening Caty saw Hedgehog by the far fence. She gave her a slow wing fan. A paw opened beside a stone. Across all that garden, the hello fitted exactly.

How many ways can friends say hello?
